learnings.summary: claude: CLI "claude" rejected flags ["--effort","low","--model","haiku","-p","--no-input"]: error: unknown option '--no-input'.
learnings.detail: Failed args: ["--effort","low","--model","haiku","-p","--no-input"]

learnings.summary: claude: CLI "claude" rejected flags ["--model","haiku","-p","--no-input"]: error: unknown option '--no-input'. Update HEADLESS_F
learnings.detail: Failed args: ["--model","haiku","-p","--no-input"]

learnings.summary: When testing two branches side by side with worktrees, dispatch two parallel agents (one per branch) instead of running everything sequentially in one thread. Each agent can set up its worktree, install deps, start its dev server, and run tests independently.

When research or parallel work is needed, ALWAYS use the DevOps Pilot orchestrator (POST /api/orchestrator/spawn) to dispatch worker agents (Gemini, Codex, Grok, etc.) instead of using built-in subagent/Agent tools. The orchestrator is the correct dispatch mechanism; built-in agents bypass it and the user cannot see the work in the orchestrator UI.

Run-Query.ps1 in DevOps Pilot takes -File (path to a .ps1 file), not -Query (WIQL string). It is a script runner, not a WIQL executor. Write WIQL logic into a .ps1 in .ai-workspace first, then pass the path via -File.
learnings.detail: Error: A parameter cannot be found that matches parameter name Query. The script just does & $File after validating the file exists.

learnings.summary: Before calling an endpoint, verify it exists in the documented API reference. Guessed routes return 404 and waste a round-trip. When a field you want to filter on is not supported as a query parameter, pull what is available and filter the rest in memory.

When merging an array with existing data read from an API, always normalize the existing value first. If the source uses an unusual separator or raw string, naive concatenation can produce a single mashed-together entry instead of separate ones. Split on the expected delimiter with a regex that tolerates whitespace, then join back with a canonical separator.

WIQL does not allow ORDER BY on the Tags field. Queries with ORDER BY [System.Tags] fail with a 400 Bad Request. Order by Id, State, or WorkItemType instead. The error body is often empty, which makes this hard to diagnose.

sendTrace and sendException have different signatures. sendTrace is (message, severityLevel=1, properties={}) -- 3 args. sendException is (exceptionType, message, method, properties={}) -- 4 args. Do not use the 4-arg exception shape for sendTrace.

The xlsx (SheetJS) library strips all formatting (colors, borders, fonts, column widths, merged cells) when you convert a sheet to an array with sheet_to_json and rebuild with aoa_to_sheet. To preserve styles when modifying an Excel file, manipulate cells in-place on the existing worksheet object: use shiftRowsDown to move cells, then write new cell values directly with writeRow copying style from a reference row. Read with { cellStyles: true } and write with { cellStyles: true }.
learnings.detail: sheet_to_json -> modify array -> aoa_to_sheet destroys all Excel formatting. Instead: (1) read existing cell addresses, (2) shift rows down from insertion point, (3) write new values into individual cells, copying .s (style) from a nearby reference row. This preserves the original workbook formatting.

learnings.summary: The SheetJS (xlsx) npm package community edition does NOT preserve styles, colors, or formatting -- even with cellStyles:true. That is a Pro-only feature. Use exceljs instead, which reads and writes xlsx files with full style preservation (fills, fonts, borders, tab colors, merged cells, row heights, column widths). When modifying existing rows, unmerge any merged ranges first before clearing/rewriting cells, otherwise merged cell values bleed into new data.
learnings.detail: Previous learning about shiftRowsDown + cellStyles is wrong -- SheetJS community cannot do it. exceljs is the correct library. Key gotcha: if the original file has merged cells (e.g. A44:F44 for a TOTAL row), you must call ws.unMergeCells(range) BEFORE clearing and rewriting those rows, otherwise the merge persists and corrupts new data written to those cells.

learnings.summary: In markdown, a blank line inside a pipe table breaks the table. All table rows must be contiguous with no empty lines between them. When inserting new rows into an existing markdown table, never leave a blank line between the old last row and the new first row, or the new rows will render as raw pipe-delimited text instead of table cells.

When extracting Elementor sections from a page to use as templates, always verify the actual column count and structure rather than relying on design doc descriptions. The design notes may describe an idealized layout (e.g. 3-col [20%,60%,20%]) while the actual implementation uses a different structure (e.g. 1-col 100%). Always inspect the JSON data before coding against it.

Elementor section background_color set via API does not render on the frontend until the CSS cache is regenerated (open in Elementor editor + click Update). For immediate rendering without cache regeneration, use the CSS viewport breakout technique on the HTML widget itself: wrap content in an outer div with width:100vw; position:relative; left:50%; transform:translateX(-50%); background:#color, and cap inner content with max-width:1440px; margin:0 auto. Also clear _elementor_css meta to force cache regeneration on next load.

When using the CSS 100vw breakout technique (width:100vw; left:50%; transform:translateX(-50%)) inside Elementor HTML widgets, always add: (1) overflow-x:clip on the breakout div to prevent horizontal scrollbar from scrollbar-width mismatch, (2) max-width:100vw as fallback, (3) overflow:hidden on the parent Elementor section via custom_css, (4) zero out all padding on the Elementor column via custom_css (selector > .elementor-element-populated { padding: 0 !important; }). Without these, mobile views get horizontal overflow and inward padding gaps.

Elementor responsive widget settings (align_mobile, _margin_mobile, etc.) written via API do NOT take effect until the CSS cache is regenerated by opening the page in Elementor editor and clicking Update. For immediate mobile fixes without editor access, use custom_css on the section with @media queries and the selector keyword. Custom CSS is embedded inline and renders immediately. This is the only reliable way to fix mobile layout via API.

Push-AndPR.ps1 breaks when -Description contains commas, apostrophes, or other special characters. PowerShell string parsing fails with TerminatorExpectedAtEndOfString. Instead, push the branch manually with git push -u origin HEAD, then create the PR via curl to POST /api/pull-request with a JSON body, which handles special characters correctly.
Builder-style image audits can produce false positives when custom components render alt text from fields such as imageAltText or imageAltTag instead of alt or altText.
learnings.detail: Before bulk editing CMS image alt text, inspect the consuming component code and treat component-specific alt fields as valid. Do not rely only on a generic audit that recognizes alt and altText.

learnings.summary: System.Drawing Bitmap.Save may throw a generic GDI+ error when saving generated images into dot-prefixed workspace folders.
learnings.detail: If this happens, save the generated image to a normal writable path, verify the file exists, then clean it up after use. Do not assume the drawing code failed before testing a simpler output path.

learnings.summary: In PowerShell loops, Invoke-RestMethod failures can leave a previous response variable in place and make later logging look like a false success.
learnings.detail: Reset the response variable before each request or wrap Invoke-RestMethod in try/catch. On catch, log the failure separately and do not read stale response data from a previous iteration.

learnings.summary: curl.exe JSON POSTs from PowerShell can hang or time out when inline body quoting is misescaped.
learnings.detail: For local API writes from PowerShell, prefer Invoke-RestMethod with a hashtable converted by ConvertTo-Json, or write complex JSON to a temp file and post that. Avoid deeply escaped inline curl JSON bodies.

learnings.summary: Node fs.writeFile can hit EPERM when writing generated files into a dot-prefixed workspace folder.
learnings.detail: If Node cannot write a generated manifest or temporary output into a dot-prefixed workspace folder, emit the data to stdout or write to another verified writable path, then clean up. Do not keep retrying the same path.

learnings.summary: When parsing markdown table rows with node -e, always guard cells.length before indexing. Header separator rows (|---|---|) split into fewer cells than data rows and cause TypeError on cells[N].replace. Skip rows where cells.length is below the expected column count.
learnings.detail: Encountered TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading replace) while parsing a markdown table via l.split(|). The offending line was a style-laden STORY row that split unevenly due to embedded HTML. Fix: add `if (cells.length < EXPECTED) continue;` before destructuring, and strip HTML with replace(/<[^>]+>/g, ) before trimming.

learnings.summary: Builder.io plugin GET /entries/:model hangs/404s; use GET /content/:model?limit=N instead. /entries is not the real route.
learnings.detail: The instructions table lists Get-Entries.ps1 (-Model), but the REST route for listing entries is /api/plugins/builderio/content/MODEL_NAME?limit=N. Calling /api/plugins/builderio/entries/MODEL never returns.

learnings.summary: Builder.io /insights?issue=missing-alt under-reports: default detector only matches alt/altText siblings. Custom field names (imageAltTag, videoAltTag, desktopImageAltTag, featuredImage without alt sibling, etc.) are missed and counts come back as 0 even when hundreds of images lack alt.
learnings.detail: For accurate alt audits on spaces with custom component schemas, fetch /content/MODEL and walk the data tree yourself. Recognize: alt, altText, altTag, imageAlt*, desktopImageAlt*, mobileImageAlt*, videoAlt*, iconAlt*, featuredImageAlt, mediaAlt*. Also handle LocalizedValue objects where each locale key may be a string URL or alt text.

learnings.summary: curl -o to a path whose parent dir does not exist fails with exit code 23 and size=0 even though it prints HTTP:200. The HTTP status is returned before write, so it is misleading.
learnings.detail: On Windows bash, shell cwd can reset between tool calls, landing in a subdir. Any relative path that assumed the project root then fails. Always mkdir -p the target dir in the same bash call as the curl, or use an absolute path. Always check curl exit code, not just the HTTP status from -w.

learnings.summary: Builder.io plugin does not expose GET /assets/:id for single-asset fetch. Calling it hangs until the bash timeout. Use GET /assets?query=... or /assets?limit=... and filter by id in the response instead.
learnings.detail: The routes module registers PATCH /assets/:id and DELETE /assets/:id but no GET. An unmatched GET path falls through to a handler that never responds, so curl hits its timeout rather than getting a 404.

learnings.summary: Builder.io plugin /assets?query=<value> can time out at 30s because it paginates through the full asset library on the Builder admin API for each call. Use a larger curl --max-time (120s+) or pre-cache via /assets full scan first.
learnings.detail: Asset search is not a real server-side filter on the Builder side, the plugin scans pages and filters locally. Short timeouts will kill the request mid-scan.

learnings.summary: Before bulk-writing alt text to a Builder.io space, verify the model schema defines an alt sibling subfield. If not, the frontend component may be reading alt from a specific custom key and a PATCH that writes altText will be silently ignored by the rendered page.
learnings.detail: A Builder.io model can have a seoFields object with only metaTitle, metaDescription, featuredImage, schemaJson subfields. The Builder UI still shows a per-usage 'Alt text for this page' input, but that writes an ad hoc field the frontend may or may not render. Always map image field to alt field by inspecting the consuming component source before bulk PATCHing the Write API.

learnings.summary: Builder.io Write API enforces Firestore document limits: PATCH returns 500 with 'Input object is deeper than 20 levels or contains a cycle' when the merged data tree exceeds 20 nesting levels. Cannot patch deeply nested page entries (often Symbol-within-Symbol layouts). Workaround: edit those entries via Builder.io UI which can flatten on save, or refactor the page structure first.
learnings.detail: Hit on a Pricing page with many Columns -> Sections -> Symbols nesting. The PATCH body itself is small, but the resulting merged document violates Firestore's 20-level depth limit.

learnings.summary: When deduping CDN image URLs by their first 12 hex chars of the asset id, you can collide. Different uploads of the same source photo share a long common prefix. Always dedupe by full URL (or full asset id), not a truncated prefix.
learnings.detail: In a bulk image audit, two different Builder.io assets started with the same 12 hex chars (9b5322c33a0d) but referenced different files. The truncated-prefix dedup map silently dropped one of them and that entry got NO-OP'd.

learnings.summary: Orchestrator's claude CLI worker can hit a circuit-breaker after a few headless task failures, blocking further claude spawns until it cools down. Symptom: 'Retry failed: CLI claude circuit breaker is OPEN'. Workaround: switch to gemini, codex, or grok for that batch of work and resume claude later.
learnings.detail: Hit when spawning 4 parallel claude workers for vision tasks. Worker tasks failed initially (likely a flag/cwd issue) and the breaker tripped, locking out further claude spawns even with corrected prompts.

learnings.summary: Bash heredoc (cat <<EOF) fails with unexpected EOF when the body contains backticks or other shell metacharacters even with quoted delimiter when piped through tool boundaries. For long markdown content, use the Write tool to create the file directly, then feed it to save-note.js --file, instead of heredoc in a Bash call.
learnings.detail: Saving a ~150-line markdown note via cat > file.md << NOTEEOF ... NOTEEOF returned: line 172: unexpected EOF while looking for matching quote. Switching to Write tool for the file, then calling node scripts/save-note.js --file, worked first try.

learnings.summary: DevOps Pilot notes read endpoint is GET /api/notes/read?name={name}, not GET /api/notes/{name}. The /{name} path returns a plain text 404 Not Found and wastes a round-trip. Also URL-encode parentheses in note names: ( is %28, ) is %29 � leaving them raw can yield an empty body depending on the shell.
learnings.detail: First attempt curl /api/notes/DYOB%203.0%20Phased%20Execution%20Plan returned Not found. Correct route per /api/instructions is /api/notes/read?name=... and parens in the name must be percent-encoded.

learnings.summary: When smoke-testing an async scheduler that can spawn external processes (HTTP calls, child CLIs), keep the test to self-contained node types only (branch, approval, state mutation). Worker/tool nodes that call out to a live server will hang the test when the server is not up, and the scheduler will stay stuck in running state rather than finishing. Prefer mocking the spawn layer or covering external-facing node types with an integration test that explicitly boots the server first.
learnings.detail: Hit while writing a smoke test for a graph workflow engine. Test defined a branch + two worker nodes and expected terminal state in ~800ms. Instead, the branch correctly took one path, but the downstream worker node blocked on an HTTP call to /api/orchestrator/spawn that was never going to resolve, leaving the run status=running forever.

learnings.summary: MCP tools are ONLY for exposing DevOps Pilot capabilities to external clients (Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, Zed). When building a new DevOps Pilot feature, the primary interaction surfaces are (1) a PowerShell or Node script in ./scripts/, and (2) a UI surface in the dashboard. MCP is additive icing on top of those, not a substitute. Do not ship a feature that is only reachable via MCP from outside the app.
learnings.detail: Rule from the project owner. Scripts are the canonical invocation path inside DevOps Pilot. UI gives visibility. MCP gives external interop. A complete feature ships all three, in that priority order.

learnings.summary: When persisting a workflow engine that has in-memory blocking primitives (Promise resolvers for human-approval gates, worker wait loops), the persistence layer must also persist the RESOLUTION state, not just the pending state. On restart, the in-memory resolver is gone, so clicking Approve becomes a no-op unless the engine re-enters the scheduler and recreates the waiter. Minimum viable fix: on load, reset any awaiting-approval nodes to pending and re-run the scheduler, which recreates a fresh waiter. Better fix: persist the approval decision to disk when the user clicks so a resumed run can skip past already-answered approvals without re-prompting.
learnings.detail: Hit while shipping graph-runs BETA. A run that hit an approval node and survived an app restart showed up in the approval modal, but clicking Approve returned {ok:true} silently and did nothing because approvalWaiters.get(key) returned undefined.

learnings.summary: Branch-skip propagation in a DAG scheduler must NOT blindly mark every descendant of the skipped node as skipped. A merge node that depends on both branches still has a valid path through the taken branch and should run. The correct rule: a node is only skipped when every one of its dependencies is already in the skip set; iterate to a fixed point so chained merges resolve. Separately: after marking skipped nodes as terminal (cancelled), the scheduler must continue re-checking ready nodes on the same pass, not break out of the loop, because newly-unblocked merge nodes need to be picked up immediately.
learnings.detail: Hit in the v1 graph-runs engine. Test graph: decide -> (big | small) -> summary. When small was skipped by the branch, descendantsOf(small) included summary, so summary was marked skipped too even though big was reachable. Separate bug: even after fixing the skip propagation, the scheduler broke out of its loop the moment it marked the skipped node cancelled, so the summary merge never got scheduled in the same pass.

learnings.summary: claude: API Error: Request rejected (429) · This request would exceed your organization's rate limit of 30,000 input tokens per
learnings.detail: Failed args: ["--append-system-prompt","You are a worker agent. NEVER use sleep commands. NEVER poll with curl in a loop. Just do the task and output the result. Do not dispatch sub-tasks to other CLIs. Do not call orchestrator APIs. Focus only on the task in the prompt.","--dangerously-skip-permissions","-p"]

learnings.summary: When an AI CLI worker fails with a class-of-error that strongly suggests switching models would help (token limit, rate limit, quota exceeded, context length, circuit breaker open, auth/key error, overloaded, insufficient_quota), the caller should automatically retry with a different CLI from the model router rather than surfacing the failure to the user. Track which CLIs have been tried so the router can exclude them. Cap attempts at 3 to avoid infinite loops. Non-retryable errors (bad arguments, permission deny, not-found) should fail fast without retry.
learnings.detail: Hit in graph-runs v1 where a 4-step test graph (number -> haiku -> summarize) failed on the summary node because Claude had hit its token limit. The engine surfaced the raw failure instead of transparently switching to Codex or Gemini. Fix: _runWorkerNode now loops up to 3 times, re-querying the model router with excludeClis on each retry-worthy failure.

learnings.summary: Removing a block from server.js that contains scattered unrelated helpers silently breaks consumers
learnings.detail: During a large handler extraction (Phase 3b), splice-deleting a line range in server.js accidentally removed handleImportConfig and sanitizeText, which were interleaved with the target ADO handlers but used by unrelated code paths. The dashboard lost /api/config/import and crashed on startup with "sanitizeText is not defined". Lesson: after any multi-hundred-line deletion in a monolithic server file, grep for every function name in the deleted block against the rest of the file before committing. A quick node --check passes because the calls are runtime-only. Also: watch for functions that appear to be topic-local but are actually generic utilities (sanitizeText, proxyHtmlImages patterns) -- move them to a clearly-labeled utility section before deleting the surrounding context.

learnings.summary: PowerShell curl alias prompts for Uri when given -s flag
learnings.detail: In Windows PowerShell, `curl` is an alias for Invoke-WebRequest. The -s flag prefix-matches -SessionVariable / -SkipCertificateCheck (ambiguous), causing PowerShell to discard the URL and prompt `Uri:` interactively. Use `Invoke-RestMethod <url>` (returns parsed JSON) or `curl.exe -s <url>` (real curl binary) to bypass the alias. Bash does not have this alias; curl -s works there as expected.

learnings.summary: Frontend caches plugin list once per page load; config changes mid-session can leave cache stale
learnings.detail: The dashboard initPlugins IIFE fetches /api/plugins once and caches the result in _loadedPlugins. Config-keyed plugins whose activationConditions.configKeys flip from unsatisfied to satisfied mid-session (e.g. user just saved their PAT) stay absent from the cached list until the next page load. Fix: refreshPluginActivation() diff after saveSettings() and auto-restart when the active plugin set changes, since contributions are injected once at startup and are not reversible live.

learnings.summary: Async prefix route handlers that return false silently consume requests in a naive dispatcher
learnings.detail: When a route dispatcher checks `if (result !== false) return;` against an async handler, the handler returns Promise<false>, which is truthy in that check -- so the request is treated as handled and no response is written. Browser hangs until socket timeout. Fix: if the handler returns a Promise, await it before the === false comparison. Symptom I saw: /api/plugins/registry + every /api/plugins/<x> non-config path hung forever after a generic /api/plugins/<id>/config async prefix handler was added; its fall-through path (`if (!match) return false;`) quietly swallowed all other prefix traffic.

learnings.summary: rightTabs contribution expects iframe HTML; dont use it for tabs whose rendering still lives in core
learnings.detail: Plugin SDK has TWO ways to own a right-column intel tab: (a) rightTabs = iframe-backed, plugin ships ui/<tab>.html, shell injects an iframe and a new closable button; (b) legacyNativeRightTabs = claim an existing hardcoded intelTab-<id> button, rendering logic stays in core. Mixing them up (declaring rightTabs when the rendering logic is still in core) injects duplicate buttons backed by broken iframes pointing at files the plugin does not ship. Same rule applies to centerTabs vs legacyNativeTabs. When migrating, change the manifest field AT THE SAME TIME as you move the rendering into the plugin, never before.

learnings.summary: Audit/readiness review requests are read-only unless the user explicitly asks for fixes
learnings.detail: When the user asks to compare branches, audit readiness, or check whether a branch is ready to merge, do not patch files or apply quick fixes. Report findings and recommendations only. If fixes seem obvious, ask before editing.

learnings.summary: DevOps Pilot /api/pull-request uses repoName, sourceBranch, targetBranch (not repo/head/base).
learnings.detail: POSTing {repo, head, base} to /api/pull-request returns 422 Validation Failed or "repoName is required". Correct payload: {"repoName":"<configured name>","sourceBranch":"<branch>","targetBranch":"<base>","title":"...","body":"..."}. Confirmed against the GitHub plugin route; response shape is {ok, pullRequestId, url, title}.

learnings.summary: Core shell instructions must be fully plugin-agnostic
learnings.detail: Core instruction files (INSTRUCTIONS.base.md, dashboard/instructions/*.md, /api/bootstrap payload) must not mention any specific plugin by name. That includes no sentences like -if the Azure DevOps plugin is installed- or -when the GitHub plugin is active-. Every plugin (including ADO and GitHub) must be treated identically to Builder.io, Sanity, WordPress, etc.: plugin-specific rules live inside the plugin folder at instructions.md and are fetched via /api/plugins/instructions on demand. The core should only describe the generic plugin system (discovery by keyword, ask before use, fetch that plugin instructions).

learnings.summary: PR description via /api/pull-request rendered as [object Object] when passed a string from Get-Content -Raw
learnings.detail: When creating a PR via POST /api/pull-request (or New-PullRequest.ps1), the description field did not render a multi-line string correctly and showed [object Object] in the GitHub PR body. After creating a PR, always verify the rendered description on GitHub. Safer pattern: keep description short and inline, or update the PR body via GitHub API after creation (PATCH /repos/:owner/:repo/pulls/:number with body field) if the initial render is wrong.

learnings.summary: git worktree remove fails with Filename too long when node_modules present on Windows. Mirror an empty dir over the worktree with robocopy /MIR first, then remove the now-empty dir, then git worktree prune.
learnings.detail: Deeply nested node_modules paths exceed MAX_PATH (260 chars) so git worktree remove --force errors with failed to delete <path>: Filename too long. Workaround: create an empty source dir, run robocopy.exe <empty> <worktree> /MIR /NFL /NDL /NJH /NJS /NC /NS to mirror (empties target), then Remove-Item -LiteralPath <worktree> -Recurse -Force, finally git worktree prune to clean the registry. Mirroring many node_modules is slow (tens of seconds per worktree), so run it in the background and poll the dir until it is gone.

learnings.summary: Codex workers spawned with cwd inside a Node project on Windows cannot invoke npm: the PowerShell shim fails with a StandardOutputEncoding error, so every npm command exits 1 immediately. Build verification via codex workers does not work on Windows.
learnings.detail: Root cause: PowerShell runs C:/Program Files/nodejs/npm.ps1 which executes node.exe without redirection, triggering the StandardOutputEncoding error. Workaround options: (1) run the npm commands from the supervisor own bash session with run_in_background and log to a file, then poll the log; (2) in the worker prompt, invoke npm.cmd through cmd.exe so the PowerShell wrapper is bypassed.

learnings.summary: For web research, dispatch codex via orchestrator — do not use the claude-code general-purpose Agent. The built-in subagent does not always have WebSearch/WebFetch available and will refuse to browse.
learnings.detail: Symptom: spawning a general-purpose Agent with a research prompt returned 'I don't have web search or browsing tools available in this environment' and produced a reasoned-from-premises answer rather than live-cited research. Fix: call Get-ModelRecommendation.ps1 -Intent web-research, then POST /api/orchestrator/spawn with {cli:'codex', model:'gpt-5.4', ...}. Codex has native web search; the model router picks it for the web-research intent. Rule of thumb: anything that needs fresh URLs or pricing pages goes to the orchestrator, never to a local Agent call.

learnings.summary: /api/bootstrap response is ~84KB and overflows tool-result buffering; also breaks Read offset/limit because Read rejects files whose total token count exceeds the cap.
learnings.detail: Calling curl http://127.0.0.1:3800/api/bootstrap from bash dumps the full JSON (~84KB). In Claude Code that exceeds the inline tool-result limit and gets persisted to a file. Subsequent Read calls with offset/limit still fail because Read validates against total file size, not the requested slice. Fix: pipe through a parser on the first call (e.g. `curl -s .../api/bootstrap | node -e "let d=;process.stdin.on('data',c=>d+=c).on('end',()=>{const j=JSON.parse(d);console.log(j.checksum, j.context.activeRepo, j.permissions.settings.mode);})"`) to extract just the fields you need, or use jq. Do not rely on reading the persisted dump.

learnings.summary: Get-ModelRecommendation.ps1 -Intent has a fixed ValidateSet; "research" is NOT a valid value, use "web-research" or "web-research-cheap".
learnings.detail: Valid -Intent values are: quick-summary, deep-code, plan-and-implement, long-autonomy, web-research, web-research-cheap, pr-review, social-live, parallel-fanout, large-context. Passing "research" fails with a ValidateSet ParameterArgumentValidationError. For online research tasks use -Intent web-research (flagship) or web-research-cheap (budget).

learnings.summary: Codex workers spawned via /api/orchestrator/spawn run sandboxed with network access disabled by default, so intents like web-research fail silently -- the task completes but the worker reports it could not run live searches.
learnings.detail: A codex worker dispatched for a live-web-research task returned: "Network access is restricted and approval is disabled, so I cannot run the required live web searches." The task state was completed (no error field), so the failure is only visible in the result text. Before dispatching codex for web-research, either (a) pass spawn options that enable network/approval, (b) route the task to a CLI with live search available, or (c) fall back to using the supervisors own WebSearch/WebFetch tools. Always inspect the result body before assuming success.

learnings.summary: Loop detected: repeated "fill_handle" with same args. Agent must detect when navigation is stuck and call finish instead of retrying.
Never guess Symphonee /api/* endpoints. The bootstrap payload already contains the full endpoint table in instructions (api-reference.md) -- grep it before calling.
learnings.detail: Concrete example: there is no /api/browser/open. To open a URL you must POST /api/browser/launch, then POST /api/browser/navigate with { url }. /api/browser/launch does not accept a url field. When you hit a 404 on a /api/* route, search the instructions section of the bootstrap response (or /api/instructions) for the real route name -- do not guess variants or grep the source code first.

learnings.summary: curl --data-binary @- with a heredoc can silently hang / return nothing on long-polling POST endpoints
learnings.detail: Running curl POST with an inline heredoc body (<<EOF ... EOF) against an endpoint that spawns a long-running worker sometimes finishes with no output and no server-side side effect. Writing the JSON body to a real file first and POSTing with --data-binary @/path/to/file.json works reliably.

learnings.summary: Windows bash /tmp is not the same path as Windows TEMP - cross-tool writes to /tmp will not be readable by PowerShell or Python scripts unless you share a common path
learnings.detail: In Git-Bash on Windows, /tmp is a per-session unixy path, not C:/Windows/Temp. Python or PowerShell commands that need to read a bash-written file should use the Windows TEMP dir (expand %USERPROFILE%/AppData/Local/Temp) or a project-local path instead.

learnings.summary: Passing a ~35KB string as an argv arg via $(cat file) triggers OS argv-length limits
learnings.detail: Node and other CLIs error with Argument list too long (or Windows equivalent ~32KB cap) when a multi-KB string is inlined via command substitution. Use a --file flag that streams from disk instead.

learnings.summary: Gemini 3.1 flash-image-preview reshuffles scene layout on non-square inputs; 1:1 edits reliably but introduces a zoom-crop regression if you pad-to-square and crop back
learnings.detail: Community-documented behavior: the model recomposes layout (wrong camera angle, missing non-wet-zone items) when given non-square images. Pad-to-square workaround causes the model to treat the padded canvas as new generation space and shrink content. Better fix: detect the input aspect ratio and pass generationConfig.imageConfig.aspectRatio set to the closest supported ratio (1:1, 2:3, 3:2, 3:4, 4:3, 4:5, 5:4, 9:16, 16:9, 21:9) so the model outputs at the native shape.

learnings.summary: Enumerated examples in preservation-style prompts can cause the model to inject those examples into the output
learnings.detail: A prompt rule like Preserve the wall, whether it is brick, stone, wallpaper, wood grain, etc. biased the image model toward rendering brick even when the input wall was plain paint. Stripping the examples entirely worsened preservation - the model needs some anchor. Conclusion: give at most one neutral example (or none), never a long enumerated list, and never repeat the same example across multiple rules.

learnings.summary: sharp.rotate() with no arguments applies EXIF orientation and strips the tag - critical for mobile portrait photos
learnings.detail: Many phone cameras store portrait photos as landscape pixel grids plus an EXIF Orientation tag. Without calling sharp(buf).rotate() (no args) before reading width/height or doing any further processing, the pipeline sees swapped dimensions and misaligned subsequent crops.

learnings.summary: JavaScript const is not hoisted - using a const arrow function inside a useCallback defined earlier compiles but throws ReferenceError at runtime
learnings.detail: tsc --noEmit checks types, not temporal dead zone. A React component that declares useCallback A which calls const B defined below will pass typecheck but fail at runtime when A fires. Either reorder so B is declared first, or use a ref pattern.

learnings.summary: CSS display:none on a parent hides all children regardless of z-index - mounting a high-z-index overlay inside a display:none element makes it invisible
learnings.detail: On mobile layouts where the desktop canvas element gets display:none via a media query, any child of that canvas (like a feedback button pill) is invisible no matter its z-index. The overlay has to be mounted inside the mobile-visible DOM tree instead, not the hidden desktop tree.

learnings.summary: FAL concurrency cap is 10 across all endpoints in an account - batch-SAM with 5 concurrency leaves headroom for mask download fetches on the same CDN
learnings.detail: A SAM text-prompted pipeline that runs 30 prompts in parallel can hit concurrency limits because mask downloads from fal.media also count. Keep the SAM fan-out to ~5 so parallel mask fetches have room.

learnings.summary: OpenAI Whisper API requires array notation for timestamp granularities
learnings.detail: When requesting word-level timestamps from OpenAI Whisper via multipart/form-data, the field key MUST be \"timestamp_granularities[]\" (with brackets) rather than just \"timestamp_granularities\".

learnings.summary: OpenAI 429 error (quota exceeded) handling in video-use
learnings.detail: The video-use plugin previously lacked OpenAI support. Adding it requires handling 429 errors gracefully or ensuring the user is aware of quota limitations.

learnings.summary: Flexible transcript resolution in video-use
learnings.detail: The video-use renderer should try both [sourceId].json and the raw sourceId when looking for transcripts in the edit directory to accommodate both stem-based and filename-based source IDs.

learnings.summary: GitHub Push-AndPR.ps1 and New-PullRequest.ps1 fail for repo names containing hyphens because they read the config object with $config.Repos.$Repo
learnings.detail: When the configured repo key contains hyphens, dot-property access returns null and the scripts print Repository not found. Use indexed/property lookup that supports arbitrary keys, such as $config.Repos[$Repo] or $config.Repos.PSObject.Properties[$Repo].Value, before pushing or creating the PR.

learnings.summary: ADO Task type rejects Resolved state; only User Stories allow it
learnings.detail: Azure DevOps Agile-process Task work items have states New -> Active -> Closed (no Resolved). PATCH /api/workitems/:id/state with {state:"Resolved"} returns 400 "value not in the list of supported values" for Task type. User Story / Bug / Epic / Feature types DO support Resolved. Before resolving in bulk, check the work-item type and use Closed for Task, Resolved for User Story.

learnings.summary: Builder.io locale is a reserved targeting attribute - must use dedicated mutations
learnings.detail: Calling upsertCustomTargetingAttribute with key="locale" returns: "The locale attribute cannot be modified using this endpoint. Use the dedicated locale endpoints (upsertSpaceLocale, deleteSpaceLocale, setSpaceLocales, etc.) instead." Use setSpaceLocales(locales: [String!]!) to replace the whole list, and upsertSpaceLocale(locale: LocaleDescriptionInput) to attach name+description. Both mutations return TargetingAttributeSchema! (not a locale object), so the selection set must be { type enum descriptions { name description } }.

learnings.summary: Builder admin SDK typed Mutation omits locale/targeting/webhook/settings ops; fall back to raw GraphQL
learnings.detail: The admin SDK exposes only model + space + folder + asset + auth-provider mutations via createAdminApiClient. setSpaceLocales, upsertSpaceLocale, setCustomTargetingAttributes, upsertCustomTargetingAttribute, updateWebhooks, updateSpaceEditorSettings, and updatePlugins are NOT in the chain/mutation type. POST raw GraphQL to the admin endpoint with header Authorization: Bearer <privateKey>. Introspect available mutations via { __schema { mutationType { fields { name args { name } } } } }.

learnings.summary: Builder admin GraphQL `settings` field is JSONObject! - no subselections
learnings.detail: The admin GraphQL `settings` field on Query has type JSONObject! (untyped JSON), so `query { settings { name } }` fails with "Field settings must not have a selection since type JSONObject! has no subfields". Use `query { settings }` and walk the resulting JSON in code. Same applies to other JSONObject-typed fields.

learnings.summary: Zod 4 removed errorMap on z.literal; use { message } directly
learnings.detail: z.literal(true, { errorMap: () => ({ message: "x" }) }) errors with "Object literal may only specify known properties, and errorMap does not exist". In Zod 4 the literal signature is z.literal(value, { message }) or z.literal(value, { error }). Use message for a static string.

learnings.summary: Zod 4 returns verbose default codes for missing required fields, not refinement messages
learnings.detail: For a schema like z.string().min(1, "required"), an absent field returns the issue message "Invalid input: expected string, received undefined" (the type-mismatch default), not "required". The .min refinement only runs on present-but-malformed values. To get short stable codes for missing fields, define the field with a refine() or use a custom error map that maps the invalid_type code to your short code at the schema root.

learnings.summary: `next build` is silent in background mode until completion
learnings.detail: Running `next build` via Bash run_in_background produces an empty output file for the entire build duration, then dumps all stdout at once on exit. Do not poll for partial progress - just wait for the exit notification. Build time on a fresh template install is ~12-20s; on a polished skeleton ~25-40s.

learnings.summary: `gh` CLI is not installed by default on Windows dev boxes
learnings.detail: Running `gh api repos/...` returns "command not found" on Windows. Fall back to curl against the public REST API (api.github.com/repos/<owner>/<repo>) for read-only repo metadata, ls-remote for ref state, and the user's local Git credentials for authenticated git push. Recommend the user install gh via winget if PR / Actions work is expected.

learnings.summary: Frameworks with trailingSlash setting return 308 on POST without slash; curl -L required
learnings.detail: Web frameworks that enforce canonical trailing slashes (Next, NestJS with redirects, etc.) issue 308 Permanent Redirect to the slash form. POST clients that do not follow redirects see only the redirect body. For smoke tests via curl, add -L to follow, or hit the canonical form directly. Affects every POST API smoke once the framework rewrite kicks in.

learnings.summary: Symphonee ADO plugin: assignment endpoint is undocumented but works via root PATCH
learnings.detail: State transitions go through PATCH /workitems/:id/state. Reassignment is not in the documented routes table but works as PATCH /workitems/:id with body assignedTo=<email>. Returns ok:true,id. The /assign sub-route returns a plugin-not-configured error and should not be used. Verify by re-fetching the item; the assignedTo field returns the resolved display name.

learnings.summary: Builder.io content API returns at most 100 entries per call - paginate via offset
learnings.detail: Even when limit=500 is passed to the content v3 read API, results cap at 100 (limit=100 is the hard maximum). To get all entries for a model, paginate using &offset=N. The X-Total-Count or equivalent count is not always exposed - the right pattern is to keep fetching with offset += 100 until results is shorter than 100.

learnings.summary: Builder.io reference field shape - @builder.io/core:Reference
learnings.detail: When writing entries via /api/v1/write/<model> that reference another model, the field value must be { "@type": "@builder.io/core:Reference", "id": "<entry-id>", "model": "<model-name>" }. Pass just the id string and the write succeeds but the reference does not resolve in subsequent reads. Same shape for list sub-fields that contain a reference.

learnings.summary: Builder.io examplePageUrl uses single-brace {field} substitution, not {{field}}
learnings.detail: The model.examplePageUrl placeholder substitution is single curly braces - {slug} resolves to the entry data.slug field at runtime. Double braces ({{data.slug}}) are NOT substituted and render as a literal string in the editor preview URL. Reference field paths use the top-level data field name (slug), not a dotted data.slug path.

learnings.summary: Builder.io data-model examplePageUrl is STATIC - no placeholder substitution
learnings.detail: Despite docs / community posts suggesting {field} or {{field}} substitution, examplePageUrl on data-kind models is a literal static URL. Neither {slug} nor {{data.slug}} are interpolated; the editor renders them URL-encoded (%7Bslug%7D). The canonical preview pattern for data models is: (1) set examplePageUrl to a static landing route; (2) Builder.io editor iframes that URL with ?builder.preview=<model>&builder.entry=<id> appended; (3) the app reads the entry id from search params and fetches by id with includeUnpublished=true. The /[slug] route can coexist for direct browsing.

learnings.summary: Builder.io editor signals entry via builder.overrides.<modelName>=<id>, not builder.entry
learnings.detail: When the Builder.io editor iframes a data-model preview URL, the entry id arrives as ?builder.overrides.<modelName>=<entryId> (e.g. builder.overrides.product=xxx), and there is a duplicate ?builder.overrides.<entryId>=<entryId> param. There is no ?builder.entry=<id> for data models - that pattern is page-model behavior. Use the @builder.io/react BuilderContent component which parses these params internally and also subscribes to live editor updates via window.postMessage. The component receives the entry data on every keystroke without a save round-trip.

learnings.summary: Builder admin upload endpoint creates CDN bytes only - asset library entry is session-only
learnings.detail: The Bearer-PAT upload endpoint stores file bytes on the CDN and returns a working asset URL, but the corresponding library catalog entry is NOT created. The admin GraphQL assets(input) query returns 0 even after many such uploads. Multipart variants and alternate REST paths do not change this. Only the editor UI picker (session cookie auth) registers library entries. For bulk-loaded content, plan to either (a) accept orphan CDN URLs that work for display but are not browsable in the picker, or (b) leave image fields empty and have editors upload through the picker for proper library registration.

learnings.summary: Builder model recreation wipes examplePageUrl and other per-model settings
learnings.detail: Deleting and re-adding a model via the admin GraphQL deleteModel + addModel mutations produces a NEW model id and resets all per-model settings to defaults - examplePageUrl, helperText drift, editingUrlLogic, custom permissions. After every model recreate, re-run any setter scripts that configure those settings or the in-editor preview iframe will be blank. Safer: use updateModel(body:{id,data:{...fields}}) when only modifying field definitions; only delete+recreate when the model is being meaningfully restructured.

learnings.summary: bash + node -e arrow IIFE inside double-quoted block syntactically breaks on the final paren
learnings.detail: When piping curl output to a node -e one-liner inside a bash for-loop with double-quoted command substitution, the closing paren of an IIFE like ()=>{...} sometimes gets eaten by the shell or interpreted as command grouping. Symptom: "SyntaxError: missing ) after argument list". Workaround: pipe to a small .mjs script file instead. The underlying HTTP requests still ran; only the parse step crashed - so always verify state via a separate read call rather than trusting the printed output.

learnings.summary: Builder.io GraphQL: createModel mutation renamed to addModel(body: JSONObject!)
learnings.detail: Builder.io admin GraphQL no longer exposes createModel/CreateModelInput; use addModel(body: JSONObject!) with the same shape {name, kind, fields}. updateModel/deleteModel are unchanged. Verify via { __schema { mutationType { fields { name } } } } against the admin endpoint.

learnings.summary: From bash tool, never put unescaped $ in a powershell.exe -Command string - bash expands $var to empty before PowerShell sees it.
learnings.detail:
Failure mode: bash double-quoted strings interpolate $var. Running
  powershell.exe -Command "$b = Invoke-RestMethod ...; @{ x = $b.checksum }"
causes bash to strip every $b, so PowerShell receives
   = Invoke-RestMethod ...; @{ x = .checksum }
and errors with: "=: The term = is not recognized" / ".checksum: The term .checksum is not recognized".
Even $var inside a JSON body passed as -d '...' is unsafe when the outer -Command "..." is bash-double-quoted, because bash interpolates the entire argument before quoting layers inside it matter.

Fixes (in order of preference):
  (1) Write the PowerShell code to .ai-workspace/x.ps1 and run
        powershell.exe -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -NoProfile -File ./.ai-workspace/x.ps1
  (2) Escape every $ as \$ inside the bash double-quoted -Command argument.
  (3) Use the PowerShell tool directly instead of the bash tool.

Single-line one-shots with no $variables (e.g. Invoke-RestMethod URL | ConvertTo-Json) are safe.

learnings.summary: Push-AndPR.ps1 and New-PullRequest.ps1 read repos from wrong endpoint
learnings.detail: Both scripts in dashboard/plugins/github/scripts/ read $config.Repos.$Repo from /api/config, but configured repos actually live at /api/repos (returns flat name->path dict). Result: every call dies with "Repository not found" before pushing. Workaround: push manually with git push -u origin <branch> then POST to /api/pull-request with body {repoName, title, description, sourceBranch, targetBranch, workItemId?}. Real fix: patch the two scripts to use Invoke-RestMethod http://127.0.0.1:3800/api/repos and index by name.

learnings.summary: Codex spawn returns quota-exceeded immediately when OpenAI account is out of credits
learnings.detail: errorClassification.failoverReason = out of credits / quota. CLI prints ERROR: Quota exceeded then exits. Not retryable. Failover to another CLI (Claude/Gemini/Grok) or have the user top up. Detected via task.error containing Quota exceeded substring.

learnings.summary: ADO work-item parent/child nesting: the create/update REST routes only set fields, not hierarchy. To nest, PATCH the CHILD with op add /relations/- value { rel: 'System.LinkTypes.Hierarchy-Reverse', url: <parent workItems url> } via the Azure DevOps REST API (api-version=7.1, content-type application/json-patch+json).
learnings.detail: Plugin create routes that wrap workitems cannot link parents. Read the PAT from the plugin config and call dev.azure.com directly for the relation. Also: an iteration node must already exist before assigning System.IterationPath or ADO returns TF401347.

learnings.summary: git add fails the whole staging if any pathspec was already git-rm'd
learnings.detail: Passing an already-removed file path to git add (e.g. after git rm) errors with fatal: pathspec did not match, and stages NONE of the other listed files. Stage edited files separately from rm'd ones, or add by directory.

learnings.summary: Workspace restrictions on high-level tools
learnings.detail: High-level tools like list_directory, read_file, and write_file are restricted to the launch workspace (Project Neo). For multi-repo tasks in Symphonee, use run_shell_command with absolute paths or Set-Location to interact with other repositories (like DYOB3).

learnings.summary: When moving a module into a subdirectory, audit every require('./x') and __dirname-relative path - they silently resolve to the wrong place; and route-handler ReferenceErrors are invisible to a require()/load-check, only surfacing when the route is actually called (the request just hangs with no response).
learnings.detail: A route-registration module was extracted into a subdir; a helper it called was left in the parent and never imported, so the call threw ReferenceError inside an async handler -> the HTTP request hung with no response and no error in logs. Load-check passed because the handler is only invoked at request time. Also an inline require('./permissions') + path.resolve(__dirname,'..') for a config path both shifted by one directory and silently fell into a catch. Fix: thread the needed root/dep in via the function signature instead of __dirname; add a test that INVOKES the handler (not just registers it).

learnings.summary: Rate limit hit mid-task. Reduce steps: prefer direct URL navigation over multi-step UI clicks. Use Haiku model for browser tasks.
A change regressed: claim on test.txt
learnings.detail: Claimed by tester on 2026-09-07 (test.txt). Checked 2026-09-07: Test failed (1): exit 1.

learnings.detail: Claimed by tester on 2026-09-07 (revert.txt). Checked 2026-09-07: revert.txt: revert commit a772074|t|Revert "edit revert".

learnings.detail: Claimed by tester on 2026-09-07 (hand.txt). Checked 2026-09-07: hand.txt: revert commit a772074|t|Revert "edit revert".

learnings.detail: Claimed by tester on 2026-09-07 (gone.txt). Checked 2026-09-07: gone.txt no longer exists.

learnings.summary: JS new Date("YYYY-MM-DD") is UTC midnight but new Date("YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM") is local time; mixing them shifts day boundaries by one day west of UTC
learnings.detail: Parse calendar days with new Date(y, m-1, d) when comparing against local wall-clock times.

learnings.summary: Never run next build while next dev is running in the same Next.js project: both write to .next and the dev server breaks (500s, missing CSS, webpack cache rename errors). Stop the dev server first, or verify with the dev server alone.
learnings.detail: Observed with Next 15 behind netlify dev. After next build the running dev server served unstyled HTML and GET / 500. Fix was to stop it, delete .next, and start it again.

learnings.summary: Netlify Functions with the Lambda-compatible handler must call connectLambda(event) from @netlify/blobs before getStore, or Blobs is unavailable in production. Also Netlify blocks builds of Next.js versions affected by CVE-2025-55182; upgrade Next before deploying.

scripts/save-note.js hardcodes port 3800, so on a server running on another port it fails with Missing or invalid API token. Post to $SYMPHONEE_API/api/notes/save with {name, content} and the x-symphonee-token header instead until the script reads SYMPHONEE_API.

Launched headless Chrome (CDP) for phone-width screenshots instead of the in-app browser; Chrome windows popped up outside the app. Use POST /api/browser/emulate/device {width,height} then GET /api/browser/screenshot. Never start a browser of your own (absolute rule 10).

Building a JSON spawn body with node -e inside a bash command line eats the backslashes of Windows paths (C:/Code/X written with backslashes became C:CodeX); spawn then fails with ENOENT -4058 because the cwd does not exist. Write the body to a file with forward slashes and post it with --data-binary @file; never inline Windows paths in node -e.

netlify deploy --build on Windows can fail with EPERM symlink errors from @netlify/plugin-nextjs when a devDependency (e.g. jsdom) ends up in the trace, because IS_LOCAL=true skips the plugin node_modules filter that a real CI build applies.
learnings.detail: Fix: patch the cached plugin file .netlify/plugins/node_modules/@netlify/plugin-nextjs/dist/build/content/server.js, adding dereference:true to its fs.cp() calls so it copies real files instead of recreating symlinks (which need admin/Developer Mode on Windows). This is local-only (.netlify is gitignored) and unnecessary once real GitHub-connected CI (Linux) builds the site.

learnings.summary: Netlify blocks deploys of Next.js versions affected by CVE-2025-55182 (next 16.0.0 included) even when the build passes; the failure shows only as 'Build script returned non-zero exit code: 2' and the real message is at the deploy-upload stage. Bump next (16.3.4 worked) before pushing.

Unsplash images fetched by photo id can be Unsplash+ premium assets that render with a tiled watermark. Before uploading stock photos, reject any id whose photo page is unsplash.com/plus and view the downloaded file; filenames give no hint (source is null on the Sanity asset).

Images with loading=lazy inside absolutely positioned cards that are moved only by CSS transform (all sharing one layout box at the canvas origin) may never start loading: the browser judges laziness on the layout box, which never changes. Use eager loading or an IntersectionObserver for such galleries. Also, percentage padding on an absolutely positioned element resolves against the containing block, not the element.

When polishing a site an owner already likes, agents must not 'improve' signature design choices (transparent corner-only navigation, right-aligned menus, intentionally sparse grids, chosen accent fonts). Pass-3 agents given generic responsive/accessibility briefs added header backgrounds, boxed corner links, padded galleries with off-brand stock, and re-aligned menus, all of which the owner reverted. Briefs must say: keep the existing design intent; fix bugs, do not restyle.

A glyph/emoji cleanup sweep must cover one wide range U+2010-2BFF plus U+1F000-1FAFF, plus HTML numeric/named entities (→ “) and CSS content: glyphs, and must be verified against RENDERED HTML of every page, not source. Hand-picked emoji blocks miss arrows (U+2190), geometric shapes (U+25A0, play triangle) and Misc Technical (U+2300, pause). Also next dev keeps stale Sanity fetches in .next; clear .next before verifying content patches.
A change was reverted: the token system in globals.css and the env-based Mapbox token stay in place and the app still builds
learnings.detail: Claimed by claude on 2026-09-08 (globals.css, ItineraryMap.jsx, .gitignore, manifest.json). Checked 2026-09-11: src/components/ItineraryMap/ItineraryMap.jsx no longer exists.

learnings.summary: A change was reverted: aleoresto.ca serves the bento UI and its functions answer 200 with persisted counters
learnings.detail: Claimed by claude on 2026-09-08 (store.js, package.json). Checked 2026-09-11: netlify/functions/_shared/store.js no longer exists.

learnings.summary: The in-app browser (/api/browser/*) is one shared webview; the session parameter is ignored and parallel agents navigate it out from under each other. When several agents screenshot in parallel, assert location.href in the same eval that scrolls, re-check href right before and after GET /api/browser/screenshot, verify the PNG dimensions (another agent may have device emulation on, producing 1280x1600 captures), and retry with short random backoff instead of long fixed waits.

unsplash.com/napi/search/photos answers curl.exe with 200 (JSON incl. premium/plus flags) but returns 401 to Python urllib regardless of User-Agent; shell out to curl via subprocess for that endpoint. Commons API imageinfo urls carry a ?utm query string, so strip before extension checks.

GET /api/browser/screenshot under POST /api/browser/emulate/device returns an image of the emulated size (e.g. 780x1688 at 390x844 dpr2) but only the real webview area (about 390x485, or 625x475 at 768) is captured and it is tiled to fill the rest. Crop to the top ~485 CSS px, scroll in 480px steps, and rely on DOM measurements (scrollWidth, getBoundingClientRect, naturalWidth) for anything below the fold or wider than 625px.

A reveal/fade-in wrapper that leaves transform, filter or will-change on the section after animating (forwards fill) becomes the containing block for any position: fixed child, so a fixed bottom bar renders inside the section thousands of px down. Remove those properties once the animation ends (animationend -> is-done class).
Netlify Next plugin fails with Failed publishing static content on Windows when a dev server runs in the same folder
learnings.detail: The plugin renames .next during onPostBuild; an open dev server holds the folder. Deploy from a detached git worktree with its own npm ci, or stop the dev server first.

learnings.summary: verify.mjs (next build + next start) ran while next dev was up on the same site: the build served stale pages (missing h1, missing hreflang) and the checks failed for no real reason. verify.mjs now refuses when the registry dev port answers; always stop the dev server before a verify or deploy.

Netlify local deploy of a Next.js site fails on Windows with EPERM symlink (the Next plugin symlinks traced node_modules such as jsdom) unless Developer Mode or elevation is on. Link the Netlify site to the GitHub repo (deploy key + webhook) and build on Netlify instead (siteforge deploy.mjs --ci).
A Sanity site page must not use the slug studio: /studio is the Sanity studio route and the page is shadowed. Use /about (or another slug) and keep the menu label.

When writing French copy under a plain-ASCII rule, keep the apostrophe elisions (l apostrophe, d apostrophe, qu apostrophe): dropping diacritics is acceptable, dropping apostrophes reads as broken French. Instruct content workers explicitly.
Netlify site names are global: createSite answers 422 Unprocessable Entity when a name is taken. Pick a more specific name in the brief rather than assuming the slug is free.

MapLibre GL 6.9 never requests tiles inside the Next 16 app (style loads, sources never load, no errors); maplibre-gl@5 works with the globe projection. Also: create the map in an effect with [] deps and read callbacks through refs, or a parent re-render rebuilds the map and drops the markers.
In-app browser screenshots tile when the emulated device is larger than the window; use {reset:true} for desktop checks and rely on DOM measurements for widths the window cannot show.
learnings.detail: POST /api/browser/emulate/device {width:1440} then GET /api/browser/screenshot returned the viewport repeated in a grid. Native viewport (1024x700 after reset) screenshots are clean; phone widths (390) also tile vertically but the first tile is usable.

learnings.summary: Git Bash rewrites an argument that starts with / as a Windows path (MSYS path conversion): --pages /,/company became C:/Program Files/Git/,/company. Prefix the command with MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 when passing URL paths.

Next 16 keeps a persisted data cache in .next/cache/fetch-cache across rebuilds: after reseeding Sanity, a rebuild still serves the old documents. Delete .next/cache/fetch-cache (or the whole .next/cache) before verify.mjs or a deploy build when the dataset changed.
learnings.detail: Seen on a SiteForge site: seed-content wrote new meta descriptions, verify.mjs rebuilt, the production server still returned the previous descriptions (curl confirmed). Removing .next/cache/fetch-cache fixed it.

learnings.summary: A shell opened by the installed Symphonee app inherits SYMPHONEE_WEB_DIST, SYMPHONEE_PRODUCT_ROOT and SYMPHONEE_HOST_KIND pointing at the installed copy; a scratch server started from the source tree (scripts/test-server.mjs) then serves the INSTALLED renderer and a rebuilt apps/web/dist never shows. Unset those three (env -u ...) before starting a dev server from source.
learnings.detail: Symptom: the served index.html bundle hash differs from apps/web/dist/index.html and a fresh build is not visible. Also: scripts/test-server.mjs deletes its temp data dir when killed, so anything installed under it (an Artemis checkout, for one) goes with it - point ARTEMIS_HOME elsewhere for repeat runs.

learnings.summary: In-app browser calls without x-symphonee-actor land on the SHARED webview other agents are driving (a screenshot came back showing another agent's page). Always send x-symphonee-actor: $SYMPHONEE_ACTOR on /api/browser/* so you get your own tab.
In-app browser screenshots tile (the page repeats in a grid) when the emulated device width exceeds the browser pane at 2x; emulate tablets with deviceScaleFactor 1 (768x700) for a single clean frame

A position: fixed element inside a header that uses backdrop-filter is positioned relative to the header, not the viewport (backdrop-filter creates a containing block); render fixed menus and bars as siblings of the header

Sanity hooks API v2021-10-04: a GROQ document webhook needs type: document and includeAllVersions and refuses isDisabled; the 400 names the offending key, so read validation.keys instead of guessing shapes
A change was reverted: the sidebar New Shell button opens a shell, and a failure to open one shows a toast instead of nothing
learnings.detail: Claimed by claude on 2026-09-10 (api.ts, store.ts). Checked 2026-09-13: apps/web/src/lib/api.ts no longer exists.

learnings.summary: SiteForge content: a link to an outside address is kind 'url' with a 'url' field, a phone link is kind 'phone'; writing kind 'external' with 'href' hydrates to an empty href and the button disappears without an error
SiteForge: legacyUrls in brief.json are documentation only; redirects need redirect documents seeded (content/redirects.json) or old addresses return 404 on the live site
Netlify free plan: POST /accounts/{id}/env refuses the scopes key (403 Upgrade your account); send {key, values:[{value, context:'all'}]} only

The Symphonee in-app browser does not render MapLibre GL: a map reaches styledata but never fires render or load, even for a stock CDN build in a fixed div (WebGL context is present). Do not debug map rendering there; verify maps in the user browser and check that the style URL and workers are reachable instead

A fixed bottom bar with padding-bottom: env(safe-area-inset-bottom) inside a fixed height shows a line of page content under it when the inset is 0; give the bar height calc(height + inset), bottom: -1px and a transparent bottom border

SiteForge harvest-site.mjs now writes the full catalog and profile shape the validator wants (sourceSite, sourcePath, files, category, screenshot, dependencies, interactions, brand, palette, typography, studio, deploy); only purposes remain to write by hand, one line per new pattern

maplibre-gl 5+ and 6 ship ESM-only with a separate worker module; inside a Next bundle the canvas mounts but never renders (no render or load event). Pin maplibre-gl 4.7.1 (single-file build with the worker inlined), which renders on OpenFreeMap tiles.
learnings.detail: Symptom: .maplibregl-canvas present, data-ready never set, no error event. The CDN has no dist/maplibre-gl.js for 6.x, only .mjs plus maplibre-gl-worker.mjs. Fix: npm i maplibre-gl@4.7.1 --save-exact; the dynamic import shape (mod.default || mod) works for both.

learnings.summary: A fixed bottom bar (position fixed, bottom 0) shows a 1px line of page under it on some browsers because the viewport height is fractional. bottom:-1px does not cure it; paint the bar colour past the edge with a ::after (top:100%, height 3rem, background inherit) on the element that carries the colour.

In the Symphonee workbench, position:fixed does NOT resolve against the viewport: .wb__view carries animation: view-in ... both, which leaves an identity transform on the element forever, and a transformed ancestor becomes the containing block for every fixed child. A panel placed at computed viewport coordinates landed hundreds of pixels off. Render floating panels through createPortal(document.body), or measure relative to the containing block.
learnings.detail: Also: a toolbar with align-items: stretch makes an inline-flex wrapper take the full row height, so a shorter chip inside it sits at the TOP of the row rather than on the icons' centre line - set align-items: center on the wrapper. Both were found by measuring getBoundingClientRect in the in-app browser rather than by looking at a screenshot.

learnings.summary: An integration that needs a model key must take it from Symphonee Settings (config AiApiKeys), never from a second .env inside the data dir. Artemis shipped reading only its own .env and every run died in the planner on auth while the UI showed 'pending' forever. Also: a status field like 'configured' must mean the thing is usable (a key is reachable), not that a file exists.
learnings.detail: Google's planner reads GOOGLE_API_KEY while Settings and Gemini's docs say GEMINI_API_KEY: map one to the other rather than asking for the key twice. And surface the daemon's own readiness probe before the action, not silence after it.

learnings.summary: A long-lived helper daemon (Artemis on 127.0.0.1:8000) survives a Symphonee upgrade and keeps the OLD build's environment, so a key added in Settings appears to have no effect: the new server finds the port reachable and never respawns it. Stop the daemon and Start it again after an upgrade or a settings change, and treat 'unmanaged and running' as a reason to restart rather than to reuse.

In the Symphonee workbench every view is rendered with key={view}, so switching views REMOUNTS the stage and any state a component held is lost - that is why a tab 'resets' when you step into a shell and come back. State that should survive belongs in the store, keyed by whatever it describes (a device serial, a repo), not in the component.
learnings.detail: Also: a checklist step must never be derived from transient state. 'terminals.length > 0' un-completes when shells close, so a getting-started chip reappeared on every launch. Latch a step once it has ever been true.

learnings.summary: save-note.js fails with EINVAL on Windows when the title contains a colon: the title becomes the filename and rename() rejects it. Use a dash.

Learnings are semantically invisible to Mind retrieval: extractors/learnings.js emits every learning as kind concept, which is excluded from RECALL_KINDS (recall.js: memory, conversation, drawer) and from the dense embedding scope (eval/dense.js DEFAULT_KINDS), so 153 learning nodes are reachable only by BM25 lexical overlap against 3647 other concept nodes. Measured recall@5 for symptom-shaped questions: 12.8 percent. The 85KB of learnings shipped in every bootstrap has been masking this - slim the payload without fixing the kind and Symphonee goes blind to its own mistakes.
learnings.detail: Found by packages/core/cjs/eval/awareness.js against gold/bootstrap-awareness.json. Fix: give learnings their own kind, add it to RECALL_KINDS and the dense kind scope, rebuild embeddings, re-run the eval before shipping any bootstrap diet.

learnings.summary: Mind retrieval quality on this corpus was limited by the embedding model, not the text: nomic-embed-text separates a relevant learning from the best wrong one by only +0.036 cosine, so relevance and coincidence are nearly indistinguishable. qwen3-embedding:0.6b gives +0.086 and lifts learnings-only recall@5 from 76.9 to 88.5 percent.
learnings.detail: Measured by packages/core/cjs/eval/embed-model-shootout.js over 149 learnings and 13 symptom-shaped questions. mxbai-embed-large 84.6, bge-m3 76.9. Before rewriting text to improve retrieval, measure the separation gap - if it is under about 0.05 the model is the ceiling and better writing cannot move recall. Swapping the global model is a separate and much larger decision: it re-embeds every vector at a new dimension and needs its own eval against gold/retrieval.json.

learnings.summary: The outcome loop was manufacturing false learnings: outcomes.ts coerced a missing file into the verdict reverted, and pinned every claim from a shell with no active repo to the workspace default repo. 54 of 90 pending claims were filed against a repository that had never contained their files, so each would have come back reverted and been written back as a learning.
learnings.detail: Fixed by re-homing a claim from its files when the default repo does not contain them, recording present[] at claim time, and answering unknown when a file was never there. A real deletion still reads reverted. Before trusting any calibration or any learning that says a change was reverted, check that the claim repoPath actually contains the files.

learnings.summary: A source file can contain a literal NUL byte (e.g. a string joined on '�'), which makes ripgrep and any 'is it binary' check skip it silently. A repo-wide rename can miss such a file and the gap only surfaces at compile time.
learnings.detail: Do not treat 'contains a NUL' as 'binary' for known source extensions. Either allowlist source extensions before the NUL check, or run a second pass that reports text files carrying a NUL and handle them byte-safely (Buffer 'binary' round-trip preserves the NUL).

learnings.summary: Boot-time data migration that triggers on an empty data directory will also fire for every throwaway --data-dir, so tests and scratch runs inherit the whole real install and blow their startup budget.
learnings.detail: Gate a one-time adoption/migration on the data dir being the DEFAULT one (no explicit --data-dir / env override), not merely on it being empty. An explicit data dir is a scratch run, a test or a second profile and always wants to start empty.

learnings.summary: A change regressed: an AI in a shell can ask Symphonee what it can do and run any of it from HTTP, MCP, the palette or the CLI, with dry runs and recorded refus
learnings.detail: Claimed by claude on 2026-09-11 (action-registry.ts, actions.ts, ci.yml). Checked 2026-09-14: Test failed (1): node --test packages/gateway/dist/concurrency.test.js. Could not find 'packages/gateway/dist/concurrency.test.js'

learnings.summary: Renaming a product across stored user data must rename PATHS as well as file contents. Notebooks, document titles and per-space state directories are often named after the brand, and config keys that point at them get rewritten by the content pass - so rewriting contents alone leaves the config naming a space whose data still sits under the old directory, and it opens empty.
learnings.detail: Do the path rename depth-first with exactly the same substitution rules as the content rewrite, so a path stored inside a data file and the path on disk land on the same string. Also rename before or after consistently, and exempt any deliberate provenance record from both passes so a re-run cannot scrub it.

learnings.summary: Rewriting stored prose during a rename destroys retrievability: searches for the old name return nothing, so a knowledge base silently loses its own history. Keep the old name in the INDEX even when removing it from the text.
learnings.detail: Expand a query carrying any former product name to include the current one and the reverse, at the single tokenizer choke point. Keep the former-name list as data with a rule against adding a name that means something else in the user's world, and keep one deliberate provenance record exempt from the rewrite.

learnings.summary: Never run a find-and-replace across a whole stylesheet to change one rule. A CSS shorthand means different things to different rules: replacing 'position: absolute; inset: 0' with 'left: 0; top: 0' collapsed four full-bleed layers (including the terminal's) to zero size, silently, because the elements still exist and are still positioned.
learnings.detail: inset: 0 is the only thing giving size to an absolutely positioned element that has no width/height of its own. There is no error when it is removed, so the failure reaches the user as a rendering bug with no console trace. Change the specific rule by matching its selector, and add a contract test asserting the layers that must fill their container keep inset: 0.

learnings.summary: Renaming a project directory orphans每 CLI's session history in a different way, and each tool must be checked separately: one keys sessions by a slug of the folder name, another records the working directory inside each transcript and lists sessions for the directory you stand in, another stores cwd in a per-session workspace file.
learnings.detail: Do not assume that migrating one CLI's history covers the rest. Check each tool's home directory for path-keyed folders and for cwd fields inside session files. Rewrite only the opening/metadata record of a transcript, never the conversation body, and match on a string specific enough to exclude a predecessor project with a similar name.

learnings.summary: Codex on a ChatGPT (subscription) account rejects model gpt-5.4 with 400 invalid_request_error, even though cli-models lists it as the codex default and the router recommends it for long-autonomy; a spawn with it dies before the first step. Use claude for long-autonomy spawns on this machine until the codex model list is fixed.

A headless claude worker streams no output until it exits (task output stays empty for the whole run), so the orchestrator UI marks a long SiteForge supervisor as stale while it is actively writing brand.json and sitemap.json. Judge liveness by the process and the run-folder artefact timestamps, not by the stale badge; for multi-hour builds prefer a visible terminal.

A Cadence restart kills every headless orchestrator worker (task marked App was restarted while task was running) and nothing resumes them. A multi-hour build dispatched headless needs a RESUME prompt that reads the run folder and continues from the last complete artefact; write it up front so the restart costs minutes, not the build.

When the Claude usage limit hits, every headless claude worker dies and the orchestrator later shows an empty task list, so a parallel multi-hour build silently stops; nothing resumes it when the limit resets. Check the run-folder timestamps after a limit message and respawn from a RESUME prompt that names the exact remaining stage.

Two SiteForge briefs written in one session both defaulted to a light ground, hairlines, one accent and big display type, and the owner read the two sites as the same design. When writing look.direction, choose the register first (loud colour rooms, cinematic dark, warm editorial, coastal organic, narrative, magazine frame, immersive scroll) and make it differ from the previous two builds; minimal Swiss is never the default.

SiteForge stage 07 passed verify.mjs on a site whose phone view had a wrapping button label in a fixed bottom bar, a menu toggle with an odd decorative mark, and a mobile menu that did not cover the viewport. The script cannot see these; the agent must read every phone screenshot (390 and 412) and measure button label lines before calling a site verified. A sticky bottom call bar is a per-brief decision, not a default.

Over-correcting a review rule breaks the next builds: after the owner rejected copied blocks, the SiteForge playbooks were rewritten to scaffold every block from scratch and keep pages quiet, and the next two sites came out identical and minimal. A rule that says what not to do needs the positive default next to it (here: start from the library component and transform it), or the agent lands on the blandest safe option.

Running two Opus SiteForge supervisors plus two Opus research agents in parallel on one Claude subscription hit the session usage limit twice in one afternoon (11:57 and 14:46), and every headless worker died each time with no resume. Budget parallel Opus workers against the limit: at most two long-running Opus agents at once, keep a RESUME note current in each run folder, and check the run-folder timestamps after any limit message.
Screenshots of Webflow exports and GSAP sections in the in-app browser come back blank or stuck on a preloader unless the entrance timelines are finished first
learnings.detail: file:// pages work in the in-app browser (POST /api/browser/navigate). A Webflow export waits on its videos before lifting the preloader (remove .animation_preloader/.preloader/.transition via eval, or shoot from the copy that has the videos); GSAP or SplitText entrance animations leave text at opacity 0 in a static capture: run gsap.globalTimeline.getChildren().forEach(t=>t.progress(1)) and inject an opacity:1 override before the shutter. In a demo page, a body background paints over an html background driven by a CSS variable.
